title: Rearrange Words in a Sentence
statement: The string `text` is a sentence: words made of letters, joined by single spaces, where the very first letter is uppercase and every other letter is lowercase. Reorder the words so that their lengths never decrease from left to right, keeping words of equal length in the order they had in `text`. Return the reordered sentence in the same format: words separated by single spaces, only its first letter uppercase.
constraints: text starts with an uppercase letter; every other character is a lowercase letter or a space
Words are separated by exactly one space, with no leading or trailing spaces

examples.name: Example 3
input: To be or not to be
examples.expected: To be or to be not

tests.name: Test 9
input: Understanding the problem is half of the solution

tests.name: Test 10
input: Xylophone is a very loud instrument when played by a child in a small room

notes:
## Intuition

This is a sort by word length where ties keep their original order, which is exactly what a **stable** sort does. The only extra work is the capital letter: it belongs to whichever word ends up first, not to the word that started the sentence. A slower way that is obviously right: list the words of length 1 from left to right, then those of length 2, and so on.

## Approach

1. Lowercase the whole sentence into `lower` (only its first letter was uppercase) and split it on spaces into `words`.
2. Sort `words` by length. JavaScript's sort is stable, so equal lengths keep their order.
3. Take the new `first` word and uppercase its first letter.
4. Join `words` with single spaces into `sentence` and return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`text = "Leetcode is cool"` becomes `words = ["leetcode", "is", "cool"]` with lengths 8, 2, 4. Sorting by length gives `["is", "cool", "leetcode"]`. `first = "is"` turns into `"Is"`, and joining gives `"Is cool leetcode"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n log n) for the sort, where n is the length of `text` (splitting and joining are linear).
- Space: O(n) for the word list and the result.

## Pitfalls

- Forgetting to lowercase the original first word: `"Leetcode"` must appear as `"leetcode"` when it moves.
- Using an unstable sort (C's `qsort`, for example) without breaking ties by original index changes the order of equal-length words.
- Splitting on a pattern that creates empty words; the input uses exactly one space between words.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `lower` | `text` with every letter lowercase |
| `words` | the lowercased words, later sorted by length |
| `first` | the word that ends up at the front |
| `sentence` | the rebuilt sentence that is returned |

narration.2: Lowercase everything; the capital letter will be placed again once the order is known.
narration.3: Split the sentence into its words at the single spaces.
narration.4: Sort by length; the sort is stable, so equal-length words keep their original order.
narration.5: Pick out the word that now comes first.
narration.6: Give that word its capital first letter.
narration.7: Join the words back together with single spaces.
